analysis.title: Global Data Centers: New constraints (inflation, financing), but capacity growth still compelling
key_insights: MS forecasts global data center IT capacity growing +180 GW (+23% pa) from 2026e to 2030e, from about 136 GW at end-2026e to about 316 GW in 2030e.
The US adds the most capacity over 2026e-2030e (+88 GW), then China (+49 GW), Europe (+12 GW), India (+7 GW), SE Asia (+6 GW) and the Middle East (+3 GW).

First bull and bear cases: bull is 377 GW by 2030e (+235 GW, 28% CAGR), bear is 240 GW (+110 GW, 17% CAGR). The bear case assumes restrictions across all Five Ps (Power, Planning, Price, People, Priority).

AlphaWise survey: energy is still the top bottleneck. Speed of access to electricity is cited by 27% of operators globally and 45% in the US. China's operators cite memory availability (29%) as the main constraint.
Over the next two years, operators expect funding (14%) and access to water (17%) to become larger bottlenecks.

Build cost inflation: operators report total data center costs up +12% over the past year and expect +15% pa over the next two years. Cost per GW rose from about $30bn in 2022/23 to a projected $50-60bn by the end of the decade.
If inflation averages +8% pa to 2030, total build cost rises about +50% in five years. MS calls the compounding effect the greatest risk from this theme.
MS projects a 70 GW US power shortfall for 2026-28 before time-to-power solutions. This falls to 43 GW net of those solutions and to 38 GW including APAC spillover.
About +20 GW of excess capacity outside the US and China could in theory host US demand (+27 GW in the bull case). Candidates are India, South Korea, Japan, SE Asia, Australia and the Middle East.

AI-related credit issuance is $471bn YTD through mid-October 2026, about 2.2x the $216bn issued in FY25. MS says credit markets are becoming more selective, but high-quality hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META) are best placed to fund the spending.
Lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds face higher funding costs. CRWV unsecured debt trades above 1,000bp, within 60bp of the CCC index. The AI CDS basket trades more than 60bp wider than CDX IG.
Data center ABS supply is slowing as higher rates make the economics harder. MS's September forecast is still $25-30bn of gross ABS/CMBS issuance in 2026, $40-50bn in 2027 and $55-65bn in 2028.

US community pushback is growing. About $156bn of projects were cancelled or delayed in 2025 and $130bn in 1Q26 alone. More than 250 projects have been delayed. Pennsylvania ended fast-track permitting and New York paused permits for 50+ MW sites.

Europe is constrained by grid and planning, with moratorium-style pauses in Denmark and Scotland and a Spanish draft Royal Decree requiring 80% renewable matching. MS expects Europe to grow about +21% pa, lagging the US and China.

US view: 43 GW utility power shortfall by 2028E. Base case US capacity is 65 GW IT in 2026 rising to 152 GW by 2030. Contracts signed in the last three months are priced about 12% higher than a year ago.
China: capacity forecast to rise from 26 GW in 2025 to 80 GW by 2030E on Rmb8.5tr of capex. Memory (HBM) and domestic GPU supply are the constraints, and power is not.
Memory prices have risen more than six-fold in a year and are a new source of build inflation. AI demand absorbs advanced memory capacity.
Natural gas pipeline stocks have underperformed on data center pushback and higher yields. MS sees entry points and prefers WMB (Top Pick), DTM and TRP.

European electrical equipment: Legrand is Top Pick. MS sees 2027 estimates as too low. Siemens Energy is preferred over Wartsila, which is Underweight. Gas turbine orders hit a record 38 GW in 2Q26, and MS thinks 2026 is the peak.

earnings_insights: No earnings results are reported. Merlin Properties said at its 1H26 results call in July that it has secured near-term equipment and has 160MW let or pre-let.
Schneider, ABB and Siemens reported data-center order growth in the triple digits in 1H26 results, and Legrand about 30%. Vertiv's Americas organic growth is above 40% over the last 12 months.
Upcoming: Siemens Energy FY26 results and new 2030 targets on 11 November. MS expects the Legrand 3Q26 print may bring higher organic growth guidance.

risk_factors: Power and grid access delays remain the primary bottleneck, especially in the US.
Build cost inflation of +15% pa compounds and may force projects to be scaled back or cost more.
Credit markets are becoming more selective. Lower-rated issuers and neoclouds face higher funding costs.
Rising interest rates slow DC securitized credit and ABS economics.
Community opposition, moratoriums and permitting delays are growing in the US and parts of Europe.
Memory (HBM, DRAM) supply constraints and prices, especially for China.
Tenant concentration at developers, for example neoclouds at about 85% of Merlin's current data center rent.
A possible 2026 peak in gas turbine orders, with a moderation in 2027.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows US power needed 2026-28 of 116 GW, less 25 GW of data centers under construction and 21 GW of available grid, leaving a 70 GW potential shortfall.
Exhibit 11 shows base, bull and bear global capacity: base 136 GW in 2026e rising to 316 GW in 2030e, bull 377 GW and bear 240 GW.
Exhibit 8 shows YTD-26 AI-related issuance of $471bn against $216bn in FY25, with hyperscaler issuance of $254bn.
Exhibit 46 shows CRWV unsecured debt trading at an average above 1,000bp, within 60bp of the CCC index OAS.
Exhibit 6 shows operators expect an average +15% increase in total DC build cost over the next 2 years.
vol_and_positioning: CDS AI basket trades more than 60bp wider than CDX IG.
HQ hyperscalers trade about 5bp wider than the IG index as of October 20, 2026.
Data center ABS new-issue yields have spiked in recent weeks as Treasury rates sold off and spreads widened.
geopolitical: Recent regional military conflict in the Middle East has raised security questions, and DCs have been targeted, which affects the region's appeal as an alternative host for US capacity.
US export restrictions on Nvidia's most advanced GPUs (Hopper and Blackwell) to China continue under a presumption-of-denial policy.
Import tariffs on electronic equipment raise US capital goods costs.
European data sovereignty is a growing theme, tied to Europe-US relations and the Draghi Report.
US state and local moratoriums and pauses on data center permits (New York, Pennsylvania, Texas audit, Ohio) and European pauses (Scotland, Denmark) are tightening approvals.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand exceeds supply for years. The base case is +23% pa growth to 316 GW by 2030e, and 99% of operators are confident or somewhat confident of meeting 2030 build targets.
tension_points.bear_case: Power, planning, price, financing and people constraints. Build costs are inflating +15% pa, credit is more selective, and US community pushback is growing. The bear case is 240 GW.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Restrictions across all Five Ps (power, planning, price, people, priority) would push capacity toward the 240 GW bear case. Easing energy, planning and supply constraints with on-time construction would point to the 377 GW bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: High-quality hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META) account for more than 75% of 2027E cash capex, have roughly AA ratings and ample debt capacity, and AI leaders see 25%+ returns on invested capital.
tension_points.bear_case: Spreads have widened, and lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds face higher funding costs (CRWV above 1,000bp). Data center ABS supply is slowing as rates rise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Credit markets failing to keep supporting lower-quality issuers, or higher rates materially changing the economics of the next dollar of AI investment.

tension_points.theme: gas turbine and electrical equipment demand
tension_points.bull_case: Data center orders are growing at triple-digit rates at Schneider, ABB and Siemens, and gas turbine orders hit a record 38 GW in 2Q26.
tension_points.bear_case: Orders may reflect pre-ordering or double-ordering. MS thinks 2026 is the peak for gas turbine orders, with a moderation in 2027, and expects power OEM capacity to be balanced by 2030.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp moderation in 2027 gas turbine orders, or constraints on data center buildouts that hit pricing per MW.

theme_stances.key_argument: Capacity growth remains compelling despite new constraints from inflation and financing, with a 180 GW increase expected from 2026e to 2030e.
theme_stances.evidence: Global Data Centers: New constraints (inflation, financing), but capacity growth still compelling

theme_stances.key_argument: The urgency to secure power is greater than appreciated, so time-to-power providers should win lucrative agreements.
theme_stances.evidence: the urgency to secure power being expressed by AI players is much greater than appreciated

theme_stances.key_argument: Credit markets are becoming more selective, with pressure on lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds.
theme_stances.evidence: credit markets are becoming more selective
